Zenodo: Add taxonomic "subject" annotation to crawl results
## Purpose
Zenodo offers authors the [option to annotate with "Subjects"](https://developers.zenodo.org/#representation): 
> Specify subjects from a taxonomy or controlled vocabulary. Each term must be uniquely identified (e.g. a URL). For free form text, use the keywords field. Each array element is an object with the attributes:
> * term: Term from taxonomy or controlled vocabulary.
> * identifier: Unique identifier for term.
> * scheme: Persistent identifier scheme for id (automatically detected).

## Context
If the author goes through the trouble of making these connections, it would be good to get them. Here is an example with "subject" annotations: https://zenodo.org/record/4741241

These "subject" annotations are not currently crawled.

## Possible Implementation (optional)
Zenodo currently doesn't seem to expose the "Subject" meta-data in the website explicitly. However, we can get this through their API, e.g.: https://zenodo.org/api/records/4741241?prettyprint=1

See also: https://github.com/zenodo/zenodo/issues/2019
</issue>

19|     Interface to extend conp-dataset crawlers.

22|     Overview
23|     ==================
24| 
25|     Any crawler created from this interface will have to crawl
26|     datasets from a specific remote platforms. This base class
27|     implements the functions common to all crawled backends, in particular:
28|     (1) verify that correct fork of conp-dataset is used,
29|     (2) create and switch to an new branch for each new dataset,
30|     (3) ignore README and DATS files for the annex,
31|     (4) create new datalad datasets,
32|     (5) publish to GitHub repository,
33|     (6) create pull requests.
34| 
35|     Method run(), implemented in the base class, is the entry point to any crawler.
36|     It does the following things:
37|     (1) It calls abstract method get_all_dataset_description(), that must be implemented
38|     by the crawler in the child class. get_all_dataset_description()
39|     retrieves from the remote platform
40|     all the necessary information about each dataset that is supposed to be added or
41|     updated to conp-dataset.
42|     (2) It iterates through each dataset description, and switch to a dedicated git branch
43|     for each dataset.
44|        (2.a) If the dataset is new, the base class will create a new branch,
45|              an empty datalad repository, unannex DATS.json and README.md and create an
46|              empty GitHub repository. It will then call abstract method add_new_dataset()
47|              which will add/download all dataset files under given directory.
48|              The crawler will then add a custom DATS.json and README.md if those weren't added.
49|              Creating the README.md requires get_readme_content() to be implemented, which will
50|              return the content of the README.md in markdown format. The crawler will then save and
51|              publish all changes to the newly create repository. It will also handle adding a new submodule
52|              to .gitmodules and creating a pull request to CONP-PCNO/conp-dataset.
53|        (2.b) If the dataset already exists, verified by the existence of its corresponding branch,
54|              the base class will call abstract method update_if_necessary() which will verify
55|              if the dataset requires updating and update if so. If the dataset got updated, This method
56|              will return True which will trigger saving, publishing new content to the dataset's respective
57|              repository, creating a new DATS.json if it doesn't exist and creating a pull
58|              request to CONP-PCNO/conp-dataset.
59| 
60|     ==================
61|     How to implement a new crawler
62|     ==================
63| 
64|         (1) Create a class deriving from BaseCrawler
65|         (2) Implement the four abstract methods:
66|             * get_all_dataset_description,
67|             * add_new_dataset
68|             * update_if_necessary
69|             * get_readme_content.
70|             See docstrings of each method for specifications.
71|         (3) In crawl.py, locate the comment where it says to instantiate new crawlers,

373|         # Script must be run in the  directory of a local clone of this fork

377|             raise Exception("Remote 'origin' does not exist in current reposition")
378|         origin_url = next(self.repo.remote("origin").urls)
379|         full_name = re.search("github.com[/,:](.*).git", origin_url).group(1)

381|         if not r["fork"] or r["parent"]["full_name"] != "CONP-PCNO/conp-dataset":

383|         branch = self.repo.active_branch.name
384|         if branch != "master":
385|             raise Exception("Local git clone active branch not set to 'master'")
